report.verdict: A weak core quarter wrapped around a transformational deal. Q3-26 revenue fell 12% YoY to €8.5m (~$9.5m) — the third consecutive YoY decline, now accelerating — and adj. EBITDA fell a third to €0.8m (~$0.9m) at a 9% margin, while the net loss widened 50% to €4.5m (~$5.0m). The substance is the 30 Sep completion of 80% of 888AFRICA (€16.4m/~$18.3m), which lifts the 2027 outlook to €85-90m revenue and €17-19m adj. EBITDA; the shares rose ~20%, but the bridge to that number runs through unaudited acquired earnings, a €10.3m deferred payment against €8.0m of (partly acquired) cash, and a CFO who left five days after the print.
summary: **Core miss, deal headline.** Q3-26 revenue €8.5m (~$9.5m), -12% YoY and -3% QoQ, against a tough +31% comp in Q3-25; adj. EBITDA €0.8m (~$0.9m), -33% YoY, flat QoQ, margin 9% (-300bps). This is the third straight YoY revenue decline (Q1 -1%, Q2 -5%, Q3 -12%) and the rate of decline is accelerating. No sell-side consensus was available; Redeye and DNB Carnegie had both cut fair values ahead of/after Q2.

**Revenue mix: recurring held, non-recurring collapsed.** Recurring revenue €7.1m (~$7.9m) vs €7.0m (+1%), now 84% of revenue vs 72%; the €1.2m YoY revenue drop is client exits (incl. the Richmond Atlantic insolvency) and €0.3m lower set-up fees, i.e. non-recurring revenue roughly halved to ~€1.4m (derived).

**Costs down 12%, not enough.** Opex ex-exceptionals and SBC €7.0m (~$7.8m) vs €8.0m, personnel-led (-€1m); >25% headcount reduction since 1 Jan, exits from the Philippines and the white-label business. Programme: €4.5m annualised delivered plus €6.0m initiated in June = >€10m annualised savings. Management says revenue now runs above operating costs and the core should break even in Q4-26.

**Below the line deteriorated.** Reported EBITDA €0.4m (-64%); operating loss €(4.3)m vs €(3.5)m; finance expense €0.1m and tax €0.1m; loss after tax €(4.5)m vs €(3.0)m. Implied D&A/impairment ~€4.7m per quarter (derived) — ~55% of revenue — reflects capitalised development and acquired intangibles. 9M-26: revenue €26.3m (~$29.3m, -6%), adj. EBITDA €1.8m (-31%), operating loss €(16.2)m, loss after tax €(16.9)m vs €(11.6)m.

**Guidance bridge — nominally 'reiterated', floor nudged up, but the core was cut in August.** FY26 combined guidance now €45-48m revenue / €5.5-7.0m adj. EBITDA (~$50.2-53.5m / ~$6.1-7.8m) vs €44-48m / €5-7m at Q2 (26 Aug) and €44-48m / €10-13m standalone at Q1 (May). Since the combined range embeds ~€10-13m of 888AFRICA Q4 revenue, the standalone core has been cut to roughly €33-37m revenue and ~€3-4m EBITDA — a halving of the May EBITDA guide masked by the deal. The division driving the uplift is 888AFRICA; the division driving the underlying cut is the core B2B platform.

**Implied Q4 arithmetic is demanding.** Guidance implies combined Q4 revenue €18.7-21.7m and adj. EBITDA €3.7-5.2m. On the Q2 call Carter pointed to ~€8.5m revenue / ~€2.2m EBITDA for the core in Q4; the balance (~€10-13m revenue, ~€1.5-3.0m EBITDA) must come from 888AFRICA. Core EBITDA stepping from €0.8m to €2.2m in one quarter is the single biggest swing factor in FY26.

**2027 outlook introduced: €85-90m revenue, €17-19m adj. EBITDA** (first full year of 888AFRICA). Against the August standalone indication (€36-37m / €8-9m), this implies 888AFRICA contributing ~€48-54m revenue and ~€8-11m adj. EBITDA (derived) — i.e. ~15-20% margin vs 13% in Q2-26. Note Carter's August verbal framing was ~€18-20m EBITDA (per casino.org), so the formal range is ~€1m lighter at both ends.

**888AFRICA terms.** 80% stake from Virtual Emerging Entertainment Ltd for €16.4m (~$18.3m): €6.1m (~$6.8m) paid at completion (30 Sep 2026), €10.3m (~$11.5m) in instalments within 10 months; no further contingent payments; management retains 20%; GiG is not obliged to keep the 888 brand. Target metrics (management-sourced, unaudited): ~$50m (~€45m) annualised NGR run-rate, Q2-26 NGR +30% YoY / +17% QoQ, 13% adj. EBITDA margin, >$1m net cash generated in Q2. Implied ~3.5x run-rate adj. EBITDA for 100% (derived).

**Several outlets state the deal 'completed in August'; the company's release says 30 September 2026.** We use the company date — it matters because it means zero P&L contribution in Q3 and only balance-sheet consolidation (cash) at quarter-end.

**Funding: €8.5m raised 26 Aug** — €2.5m (~$2.8m) directed SDR issue at SEK 1.725 (~9% dilution; SDRs to 176.9m) taken by the MJ and ZJ Foundations and the CEO, plus €6.0m (~$6.7m) two-year convertible loans at 15% p.a. (lenders: Carter, Myrild AS, Nalavio Ltd), 25% convertible every six months at a 10% discount to 10-day VWAP. Cash interest ~€0.9m (~$1.0m) p.a.; conversion mechanics are structurally dilutive.

**Liquidity is the bear case.** Group cash €8.0m (~$8.9m) at 30 Sep 'reflecting the consolidation of 888AFRICA' — i.e. it includes the target's cash; the core's own cash is probably ~€4-5m (our estimate: €3.5m + €8.5m raised − €6.1m upfront − Q3 burn). Against that sit €10.3m of deferred consideration due by ~Jul-27, ~€0.9m p.a. of convertible coupon and a core that has not yet printed a cash-positive quarter. Net debt/leverage not disclosed in the sources read [unverified].

**Commercial momentum is real but small.** One new partner signed and one extension (Luckydays three-year platform renewal); three brand launches in Q3, all in Alberta with existing partners (market opened July; LuckyDays live on day one, 15 Jul). Post-quarter: PowerPlay went live in Alberta (8 Oct, first SportX deployment in the province) and River Cree Resort & Casino signed as the fifth Alberta brand (Oct). CoreX certified for Spain (20 Jul), where partners hold ~9% combined share.

**Governance: CFO out five days after results.** Phil Richards (CFO since Jul-24) left effective 2 Nov 2026 to become CFO of Chaos; a search is under way with interim arrangements. Offsetting signal: CEO Richard Carter bought 294,704 shares on 28-30 Oct, after 1.5m shares in September (holding ~5.1m before the latest purchase), and he is both an equity subscriber and a convertible lender.

**Share reaction: +19.6% to SEK 3.23** on 28 Oct (320,793 SDRs traded; next.io cited >22% intraday), from SEK 2.70, versus SEK 1.38 after the August Q2/deal announcement; still ~-31% YTD. Market cap roughly €50m, EV ~€55m before deferred consideration (MarketScreener).

**Strategic read-through: B2B pure-play becomes a B2C-led group.** Management now describes 888AFRICA as the 'high-growth second engine'; in reality on 2027 numbers it would be ~55-60% of revenue and more than half of EBITDA. Points to underwrite: channel conflict with African B2B prospects, 20% minority leakage on the best asset, FX (MZN/AOA/TZS alongside existing ARS exposure), and whether a sub-scale platform business with ~€36m revenue can sustain 23-25% margins as implied for 2027.

**Disclosure gaps.** The headline release gives no product (platform vs sportsbook) or geographic split, no EPS, and no balance-sheet/cash-flow detail; 888AFRICA figures are management-sourced; secondary coverage shows 9M-25 adj. EBITDA as €2.8m vs the company's €2.6m (we use the company figure). The full interim PDF could not be opened within this exercise.

**Thesis.** The equity is now a levered bet that 888AFRICA's growth and cash conversion fund the €10.3m deferred payment while the core reaches breakeven; if the 2027 guide is delivered, the stock trades at roughly 3-4x EV/EBITDA on attributable earnings (our rough estimate incl. deferred consideration and minorities). If the core Q4 step-up slips, a further raise — likely via the discounted convertibles — is the base case.

segments.name: Core B2B platform & sportsbook (GiG standalone)
segments.headline: Recurring base held at €7.1m but non-recurring halved; opex -12% could not offset a -12% top line, leaving adj. EBITDA at €0.8m/9% for a second quarter and a Q4 breakeven promise doing the heavy lifting.
narrative: GiG reports a single B2B operating segment (platform, sportsbook, data and managed services), and neither the headline release nor the coverage we could access gives a product or geographic split, so the analysis below is at segment level. Revenue fell 12% YoY to €8.5m (~$9.5m) and 3% QoQ from €8.8m (~$9.8m), lapping a quarter in which revenue had grown 31%. Management attributes the decline primarily to client exits — chiefly the insolvency of Richmond Atlantic, which had already triggered a €3m bad-debt provision in Q2 — and to €0.3m (~$0.3m) of lower set-up fees. The recurring line was marginally higher at €7.1m (~$7.9m) versus €7.0m, which puts recurring at 84% of revenue against 72% a year ago; by subtraction, non-recurring revenue roughly halved to ~€1.4m (~$1.6m) from ~€2.7m (~$3.0m). They want the business judged on recurring revenue, and on that basis the picture is flat rather than falling — but flat recurring revenue after a year of go-lives in Ontario and Alberta and a 31% prior-year comp implies that churn (Richmond Atlantic, the Philippines exit, the white-label wind-down) is absorbing essentially all of the new-business ramp.

Operating expenses excluding exceptional items and share-based payments fell to €7.0m (~$7.8m) from €8.0m (~$8.9m), a 12% reduction almost entirely from personnel (-€1m) after the January redundancies; the CFO said headcount is down more than 25% since 1 January, with AI and operational efficiencies 'protecting delivery', and that more savings are to come. Implied cost of sales is ~€0.7m (~$0.8m, ~8% of revenue; derived from revenue less opex less adj. EBITDA). Even so, adj. EBITDA came in at €0.8m (~$0.9m), down 33% YoY and flat QoQ, at a 9% margin (12% in Q3-25, 9% in Q2-26); the 9M margin is 7% versus 9%. Reported EBITDA was €0.4m (~$0.4m, -64%), the €0.4m gap to adjusted being SBC, termination and acquisition-related items (versus only €0.1m of adjustments a year ago — the adjustment load is rising as the restructuring and the deal costs flow through). Below EBITDA, ~€4.7m of D&A and impairment (derived) took the operating loss to €(4.3)m (~$(4.8)m) from €(3.5)m, and after €0.1m of finance cost and €0.1m of tax the loss after tax was €(4.5)m (~$(5.0)m), 50% wider YoY though narrower than Q2's €(7.2)m which carried the bad-debt provision. The D&A burden — more than half of revenue — is the legacy of capitalised development and the Sportnco intangibles and will keep IFRS earnings deeply negative even if the EBITDA line turns.

Commercially, the quarter was about Alberta. The province's regulated market opened in July; GiG secured AGLC registration and took LuckyDays live on day one (15 July), and the release counts three brand launches in the quarter, all in Alberta and all with existing partners, alongside one new partner signed and one extension to an existing agreement (Luckydays' three-year platform renewal was announced in the period). Post-quarter, PowerPlay went live in Alberta on 8 October — the first SportX sportsbook deployment in the province, using the same PAM/SportX/RulesX/DataX stack as in Ontario — and River Cree Resort & Casino (Enoch Cree Nation) signed in mid-October as the fifth Alberta brand, taking the full end-to-end stack. In Europe, CoreX was certified for Spain on 20 July, where management says partners generate an estimated 9% combined market share. Management frames these as a 'contracted pipeline of go-lives' delivering committed recurring revenue in 2027 and beyond; the problem is that none of it is yet visible in the recurring line, and Alberta launches with existing partners carry little or no set-up fee.

On outlook, the standalone business is now expected to break even in Q4-26 and to be cash generative by year-end; Carter's formulation is that with revenue running above operating costs, incremental revenue flows through to cash. The guidance arithmetic requires more than breakeven: FY26 combined adj. EBITDA of €5.5-7.0m less 9M of €1.8m implies €3.7-5.2m in Q4, and on the Q2 call Carter pointed to roughly €8.5m of revenue and €2.2m of EBITDA for the core in Q4 (with 888AFRICA supplying the rest). Stepping from €0.8m to ~€2.2m of quarterly EBITDA on flat revenue requires the full >€10m annualised savings programme (~€2.5m per quarter) to be in the Q4 run-rate with no offsetting churn — plausible on paper given the June tranche, but we would underwrite €1.3-1.7m rather than €2.2m until it is printed. The August indicative standalone outlook for 2027 (€36-37m revenue, €8-9m adj. EBITDA, €3-4m cash flow) was not withdrawn but is now folded into a combined number; at face value it implies a 23-25% margin on a business that has never exceeded 12% in any quarter we can see.

Our read: the core is being run for cash rather than growth, which is the right call given the balance sheet, but the equity story for the platform now rests on three things — Alberta/Ontario go-lives converting to recurring revenue in H1-27, no further client failures of Richmond Atlantic scale, and the Q4 cost run-rate holding. The lack of a product/geographic split means investors cannot see whether sportsbook (SportX) is gaining share within the mix or whether Spain and Canada are offsetting attrition in legacy Malta-licensed accounts; that opacity is a discount factor in its own right.

segments.name: 888AFRICA (B2C — Mozambique, Angola, Tanzania; 80% owned, consolidated from 30 Sep 2026)
segments.headline: The 'second engine' is already the bigger one: ~$50m NGR run-rate, +30% YoY, 13% margin and cash-generative — bought at ~3.5x run-rate EBITDA, but with €10.3m still to pay and every number so far management-sourced.
narrative: GiG completed the acquisition of an 80% stake in 888AFRICA from Virtual Emerging Entertainment Limited on 30 September 2026, after an agreement in principle on 25-26 August and a binding SPA on 28 September; the incumbent management team retains 20%, which Carter describes as highly aligned. Total consideration is €16.4m (~$18.3m): €6.1m (~$6.8m) paid at completion and €10.3m (~$11.5m) in instalments within ten months, with no further contingent payments. There is no obligation to continue using the 888 brand. Because closing fell on the last day of the quarter, there is no revenue or EBITDA contribution in Q3 — the only visible effect is the jump in group cash to €8.0m (~$8.9m) from €3.5m, which the release explicitly attributes to consolidating the target. We note several outlets say the deal closed 'in August'; the company's own date is 30 September.

What was bought, on GiG's presentation numbers: an operator with a market-leading position in Mozambique and licensed operations in Angola and Tanzania, launched in late 2022, running at approximately $50m (~€45m) of annualised NGR, with Q2-26 NGR up 30% YoY and 17% QoQ (one source says 19%), an adjusted EBITDA margin of 13% and more than $1m (~€0.9m) of net cash generated in the quarter. On the Q2 call management also cited 'total revenue' rising 32% from €11.3m in Q4-25 to €14.8m in Q2-26; that figure sits above the NGR run-rate and is probably a gross (pre-bonus) measure, so we would not annualise it — the basis was not clarified in the sources we read. Taking $50m NGR at a 13% margin gives ~$6.5m (~€5.8m) of run-rate adj. EBITDA; grossing the 80% price to 100% (€20.5m) implies roughly 3.5x run-rate EBITDA and ~0.45x NGR, which is cheap by European B2C standards and reflects the jurisdictional, FX and counterparty risk being taken on. 888AFRICA's stated ambition is a top-three position among African online operators by revenue and profit within five years, including M&A beyond its three current markets.

The forward numbers rest on this asset. For Q4-26 the combined guidance implies 888AFRICA contributing ~€10-13m (~$11-14.5m) of revenue and ~€1.5-3.0m of adj. EBITDA (derived: combined Q4 €18.7-21.7m / €3.7-5.2m less the ~€8.5m / ~€2.2m core indication). For 2027, group guidance of €85-90m revenue and €17-19m adj. EBITDA less the August standalone indication of €36-37m / €8-9m leaves ~€48-54m (~$54-60m) and ~€8-11m (~$9-12m) for 888AFRICA — i.e. revenue growth of ~10-20% on the $50m run-rate and margin expansion to ~17-20% from 13%. The growth assumption looks conservative relative to the +30% trajectory; the margin assumption is the stretch, and it depends on the cost actions management says are already taking effect plus the platform cost synergy of moving the operator onto GiG's own stack over time. Twenty percent of whatever is delivered accrues to the minority, so attributable adj. EBITDA from 888AFRICA in 2027 is ~€6.5-9m on these numbers.

Funding is the pressure point. The €8.5m raise (equity at SEK 1.725 plus €6m of 15% two-year convertibles, 25% convertible each half-year at a 10% discount to VWAP) covered the €6.1m upfront payment with ~€2.4m to spare; the €10.3m deferred balance has to come from 888AFRICA's own cash generation (>$1m per quarter in Q2, so perhaps €3-5m over the ten-month window), the core turning cash positive, and whatever is left of the €8.0m group cash — of which we estimate only ~€4-5m sits in the core. That leaves little room for a weak quarter on either side, and the convertible structure means the marginal euro of equity is raised at a discount to a share price that has already been reset. FX adds a layer: Mozambican metical, Angolan kwanza and Tanzanian shilling earnings consolidated into euro reporting, on top of existing Argentine peso exposure in the B2B book.

Our read: the price paid is attractive if the numbers are real and the regulatory footing in Mozambique holds, and the early evidence (cash generation, management rollover, CEO co-investing) is supportive. But the market has effectively been asked to capitalise unaudited target earnings on the strength of a slide deck; the first consolidated quarter (Q4-26, reported in February 2027) — NGR, promo intensity, margin, cash conversion and the instalment schedule — is the first real datapoint. We would also watch for channel conflict: GiG sells its platform to African operators, and now owns one.

highlights.text: **Recurring revenue held at €7.1m (~$7.9m), +1% YoY, now 84% of the mix** despite the Richmond Atlantic insolvency and exits from the Philippines/white-label — the base the 2027 core guide is built on did not shrink.

**Opex ex-exceptionals -12% YoY to €7.0m (~$7.8m); >€10m (~$11.2m) annualised savings enacted (€4.5m delivered + €6.0m initiated in June); headcount >25% lower since 1 Jan.** Core guided to breakeven in Q4-26 and cash generative by year-end.

**888AFRICA closed at ~3.5x run-rate EBITDA (derived) for a #1 operator in Mozambique growing NGR 30% YoY, 13% margin, >$1m quarterly net cash**; management rolled 20%, no earn-outs, no brand-licence dependency on 888.
**FY27 outlook of €85-90m revenue / €17-19m adj. EBITDA (~$94.8-100.4m / ~$19.0-21.2m)** roughly doubles revenue and triples EBITDA versus FY26 guidance; FY26 floor nudged up to €45m / €5.5m.

**Alberta footprint built in one quarter: three launches in Q3, five partners by mid-October (LuckyDays day-one, Casino Time, PowerPlay incl. first SportX deployment, River Cree) plus Luckydays 3-year renewal and CoreX Spain certification** — a contracted pipeline for 2027 recurring revenue.
**Group cash €8.0m (~$8.9m) vs €3.5m at June and €4.7m a year ago**, and the shares +19.6% on the day — the market gave credit for the strategic reset.
**Insider alignment: CEO bought 294,704 shares on 28-30 Oct after 1.5m in September, and personally funded both the equity placing and the convertible** alongside the two largest holders.

lowlights.text: **Revenue -12% YoY to €8.5m (~$9.5m), -3% QoQ — third consecutive YoY decline and accelerating (Q1 -1%, Q2 -5%, Q3 -12%)**; non-recurring revenue roughly halved and client churn is absorbing all new-business ramp.

**Adj. EBITDA €0.8m (~$0.9m), -33% YoY, 9% margin for a second quarter; implied standalone FY26 EBITDA has gone from €10-13m (May) to ~€3-4m (derived) — a halving masked by presenting 'combined' guidance.**
**Loss after tax -50% to €(4.5)m (~$(5.0)m); 9M €(16.9)m (~$(18.8)m) vs €(11.6)m; ~€4.7m/quarter of D&A keeps IFRS earnings deeply negative regardless of EBITDA progress.**

**CFO Phil Richards left five days after the print (effective 2 Nov) with a search only just initiated**, at the moment the group must integrate a B2C business, pay €10.3m of deferred consideration and manage a convertible.

**Funding gap: €10.3m (~$11.5m) due within 10 months plus ~€0.9m p.a. of 15% coupon, against €8.0m of group cash of which only ~€4-5m (est.) is the core's; the convertibles convert at a 10% discount to VWAP** — further dilution is the base case if Q4 slips.

**Guidance arithmetic requires combined Q4 adj. EBITDA of €3.7-5.2m (~$4.1-5.8m) vs €0.8m delivered by the core in Q3, including a core step-up to ~€2.2m** — the biggest single execution risk in FY26.

**Disclosure thin and 888AFRICA numbers unaudited: no product/geographic split, no EPS or balance-sheet detail in the headline release, secondary sources disagree on the deal's completion date and 9M-25 EBITDA; strategic pivot from B2B pure-play to B2C creates channel conflict and 20% minority leakage.**

forecast.intro: The guidance bridge has three steps. In May (Q1), standalone FY26 guidance was €44-48m revenue and €10-13m adj. EBITDA. In August (Q2), alongside the 888AFRICA announcement, this became a combined €44-48m / €5-7m assuming a full Q4 contribution from the target — which, because ~€10-13m of Q4 revenue now comes from 888AFRICA, amounted to cutting the core to ~€33-37m revenue and ~€3-4m EBITDA. In October (Q3) the combined range was 'reiterated' with the floor raised to €45m / €5.5m (~$50.2m / ~$6.1m), reflecting deal certainty and 888AFRICA's growth rather than any improvement in the core. A formal FY27 range of €85-90m / €17-19m (~$94.8-100.4m / ~$19.0-21.2m) was added; against the August standalone indication (€36-37m / €8-9m) it implies ~€48-54m / ~€8-11m from 888AFRICA, and sits ~€1m below the €18-20m EBITDA Carter had floated verbally in August.
forecast.view: **Q4-26 (our estimate):** combined revenue ~€19-21m (~$21-23m) — core ~€8.3-8.7m on flat recurring revenue and minimal set-up fees, plus 888AFRICA ~€10.5-12m at the $50m run-rate with modest growth; combined adj. EBITDA ~€3.0-4.0m (~$3.3-4.5m), assuming core €1.3-1.7m (not the ~€2.2m indicated) and 888AFRICA €1.5-2.3m at 13-19%. That puts **FY26 revenue at ~€45-47m, inside the range, but adj. EBITDA at ~€4.8-5.8m — at or just below the €5.5m floor**; the risk is skewed to the low end because the core's cost run-rate has to drop a further ~€1m per quarter with no churn offset. **FY27:** we would model revenue of ~€82-88m (core flat at ~€35-36m as Alberta/Spain go-lives offset attrition; 888AFRICA ~€47-52m on 10-15% NGR growth, i.e. we assume growth decelerates from +30%) and adj. EBITDA of ~€13-16m (~$14.5-17.8m) versus guidance of €17-19m — our gap is the core margin, where we assume ~17-20% rather than the 23-25% implied, and 888AFRICA at ~16-18%. Attributable adj. EBITDA after the 20% minority is ~€11-14m. **Leverage/liquidity direction: worse before better.** Net debt rises mechanically as the €10.3m deferred consideration is paid out of cash through Jul-27 while €6m of 15% convertibles sit on the balance sheet; we expect at least partial conversion (dilutive at a 10% VWAP discount) and would not rule out a further equity raise in H1-27 if Q4 core EBITDA prints below ~€1.5m. **IFRS earnings** stay negative through 2027 on ~€18-19m of annual D&A plus acquisition amortisation and purchase-price allocation on 888AFRICA. **Valuation sense-check (rough):** at ~€50m market cap and ~€55m EV before deferred consideration, adding €10.3m of deferred payments and adjusting for minorities gives ~4-5x our FY27E attributable EBITDA and ~3.5-4x on guidance — undemanding if delivered, but the delivery risk is concentrated in a business the market has not yet seen a consolidated quarter from. **Swing factors:** the Q4 core cost run-rate; 888AFRICA NGR growth and promo intensity in its first consolidated quarter; MZN/AOA/TZS FX; any further client insolvency; timing of Alberta go-lives (River Cree) converting to recurring revenue; the convertible conversion schedule; and the CFO appointment.
watch: Q4-26 print (Feb 2027): core adj. EBITDA vs the ~€2.2m indication and whether the core is cash-positive; first consolidated 888AFRICA quarter — NGR, margin, net cash generated, and the GGR-vs-NGR revenue basis.

Deferred consideration: cadence of the €10.3m instalments through ~Jul-27 and the cash source (888AFRICA dividends/upstreaming vs core cash vs new financing); any conversion notices on the €6m 15% convertibles and resulting dilution.
CFO succession: permanent appointment and whether interim arrangements affect the FY26 audit and first consolidated accounts for 888AFRICA (PPA, goodwill, NCI).

Core commercial conversion: River Cree and further Alberta go-lives, Spain CoreX migrations, and whether recurring revenue moves above €7.1m in Q4/Q1; any further client exits or bad-debt provisions after Richmond Atlantic.

Disclosure improvements: product (platform/sportsbook) and geographic revenue split, EPS, cash-flow statement and net debt in the Q4 report — and clarification of the FY27 standalone vs 888AFRICA split.
African regulatory and FX developments in Mozambique, Angola and Tanzania; evidence of channel conflict with GiG's B2B African prospects.
Share-count creep: SDRs at 176.9m post-placing, plus LTIP issuance and convertible conversions.
